newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound edges down on week.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound edges down on week.

text.p: The Lebanese pound edged closer to the upper end of the central bank's bid-offer intervention band in the week ended on Friday amid continued demand for U.S. dollars on the Beirut foreign exchange market, dealers said.
The dollar traded in inter-bank trade in a range of 1,539-1,542.5 pounds compared with 1,538-1,541 last week and 1,536-1,537.5 the week before, they said.
This was near the upper end of the intervention band which the Bank of Lebanon lowered during the week to 1,535.5-1,544 pounds per dollar from last week's 1,535.5-1,545.
"I think the highest deal during the week was 1,542.5, but 1,543 was the highest price quoted," a dealer who asked not to be identified told Reuters.
He said there was some supply of dollars and the market was balanced.
"We didn't reach (top end of) the Bank of Lebanon rate. I don't think anyone bought dollars from the central bank," he said.

Dealers said last week restrictions of allocations of shorter-term pound-denominated treasury bills by the central bank were helping to boost demand for dollars as investors who were allowed to buy only a small fraction of the bills they bid for changed their excess funds back to dollars.
On Friday, dealers said there was no change of trend on the market on which the Lebanese pound has steadily appreciated against the U.S. currency for the past five years.

However, the dollar was routinely in over-supply for several months until early June and traded for weeks in a tight range of a few dozen piastres at the bottom of the central bank's intervention rate.
Asked why the dollar was now more in demand, a dealer said restrictions on t-bill allocations were still affecting the market and there was some political tension.

This appeared a reference to controversy over the government's June 10 decision to raise import duties on cars and ban imports of some food products from October in a bid to reduce the heavy trade deficit and stimulate local agriculture.
